questions.label: Which city is closest to your home?

programs.name: Red Deer smart thermostat rebate
programs.rules: ENERGY STAR certified smart thermostat. One per utility account, bought in the same calendar year. Apply by December 31, 2026 or until funds run out.

programs.name: EPCOR Peak Rewards pilot
programs.rules: $50 prepaid card to enrol a thermostat you already own, plus $25 a season. Needs central AC and is limited to select Edmonton neighbourhoods. There are no free thermostats.

programs.name: Utility heat pump rebates (ENMAX, ATCO, EPCOR, FortisAlberta)
programs.rules: We found no current rebate on the utilities' own pages, so we list no amount. Ask your utility before you buy.

programs.name: Utility solar incentives
programs.rules: We found no current utility solar incentive on the utilities' own pages. Ask your utility before you buy.

programs.name: Calgary Clean Energy Improvement Program
programs.rules: Financing, not a rebate: up to 100% of cost over up to 20 years, repaid on your property tax bill. Intake is closed until winter 2026/2027.

programs.name: Calgary Home Upgrades Program
programs.rules: Free furnaces, insulation and air sealing for income-qualified Calgarians, run by Kambo Energy Group. There is a waitlist.

programs.name: St. Albert Clean Energy Improvement Program
programs.rules: Financing up to 100% of cost. Waitlist applications only, processed first come, first served.

programs.name: St. Albert CEIP incentive
programs.rules: A $1,400 incentive applied to the Clean Energy Improvement Tax per project. Minimum project $3,000. Waitlist only.

programs.name: Edmonton Clean Energy Improvement Program
programs.rules: Edmonton's residential loan is listed by Alberta Municipalities. We could not confirm the rate or whether intake is open, so check with the City.

programs.name: National Heat Pump Rebate (federal, not open yet)
programs.rules: Announced October 8, 2026 and expected to launch in early 2027. $10,000 is for households below the median income and $2,000 for other eligible homeowners. The income line and eligible homes are not published, so this is shown but not added to your total.

notes: Alberta is not part of the federal Canada Greener Homes Affordability Program.
Amounts are the most a program pays. Your rebate depends on the equipment and your final invoice.
